ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Judge a provider against what is expected under comparable conditions — never one fixed baseline. But expected traffic fluctuations must never excuse violations of the provider's safety guarantees. Seasonality explains predictable changes in operational behavior. Maintenance explains a declared, bounded operating condition. Neither proves that duplicate effects, lost guarantees, or stale-authority execution are acceptable.

change detection — has the expected-vs-observed relationship materially changed?; hard contract invariants — did the provider violate a qualified guarantee regardless of conditions? — the first two statistically calibrated, the third requiring independently verified evidence and never relaxed for busy periods or maintenance); like-with-like comparison (BetaBinomial conditional model on contextual inputs: hour/weekday/month/holiday calendar, volume/burst/concurrency, endpoint/region/account/version, request type/payload/retry status, verified maintenance state, client deployment/routing changes — with the causal-dependency warning: never condition on variables that are themselves consequences of provider failure, e.g. retry surges; baselines use independently justified context with explicit causal modeling); the four worked examples (Monday overnight 0.8% vs 0.1–1.2% ⇒ normal; Friday peak 9% vs 5–11% ⇒ normal seasonal; Friday regression 16% vs 5–11% ⇒ material contextual anomaly, investigate; verified maintenance 17% vs 12–20% with no contract violations ⇒ expected availability degradation, recovery safeguards maintained — a fixed 5% threshold false-alerts on normal Fridays, a fixed 20% misses the overnight regression); maintenance as a verified operating state (his MAINT-042 record: provider notice receipt, bounded interval, affected regions/endpoints, declared effects, idempotency_guarantee_changed flag, verification status — verify notice/scope/impact/interval before applying the maintenance baseline; post-incident announcements never rewrite earlier observations; during maintenance keep availability alerting, outcome reconciliation, and safety enforcement SEPARATE — notification suppression is not proof suppression; undeclared extensions trigger renewed investigation; consequential guarantee changes need separate qualification even during maintenance); the three recurring-change kinds (calendar seasonality ⇒ qualified baseline; workload regime change ⇒ investigate and establish a new baseline; provider behavioral drift ⇒ investigate with competing explanations preserved — examine own routing/SDK/retries/quotas/concurrency alongside provider evidence); the anti-normalization rule (frozen qualification reference vs adaptive operational forecast — the forecast explains patterns but never replaces the contract; material forecast-vs-reference divergence is itself a review event; training hygiene excludes confirmed outages, anomalous periods, unqualified maintenance, unresolved changes — never silently relabeled healthy; new patterns become baselines only with sufficient evidence and accepted calibration revision); independent corroboration before attribution (his six-row investigation table: synthetic canaries, matched endpoint/region, client config comparison, provider status records, independent effect ledger, logical-operation identity comparison — controls genuinely comparable; competing causes undistinguished ⇒ CONTEXTUAL_ANOMALY_UNATTRIBUTED, never false provider-drift); the S1–S10 adversarial fixtures (normal Friday spike ⇒ EXPECTED_SEASONAL_VARIATION; spike + genuine regression ⇒ CONTEXTUAL_ANOMALY; verified maintenance + expected latency ⇒ MAINTENANCE_CONSISTENT; maintenance + duplicate effects ⇒ CONTRACT_VIOLATION; extended maintenance ⇒ REVIEW_REQUIRED; client release doubling volume ⇒ WORKLOAD_REGIME_CHANGE; client release changing retry identities ⇒ INTEGRATION_DEFECT; slow degradation stabilizing ⇒ never silently normalize; peak-concurrency-only misbehavior ⇒ detect in scope; missing peak data ⇒ INSUFFICIENT_OBSERVABILITY) with S2 (seasonality hiding a real regression) as the crown jewel — identical peak traffic, healthy vs defective histories, detector accepts one and investigates the other, repeated during maintenance, plus one verified duplicate effect requiring immediate withdrawal regardless of context; conditional false-alert rates across calendar conditions (quiet vs peak, weekday vs weekend, holidays, maintenance vs ordinary, deployment periods, volume scopes — a 1% aggregate rate hiding 15% Friday-evening false alerts is not calibrated; rolling forward-in-time validation; timezone/DST treatment; sparse categories keep wider uncertainty). The Contextual Drift Integrity Law. intelligence.essence: Contextual Drift Integrity Law: NayaNET shall evaluate operational anomalies against independently qualified temporal, workload and maintenance context. Expected patterns may adjust statistical expectations and notification routing but cannot weaken safety invariants, change LAW authority, or establish external guarantees. Adaptive baselines must not silently normalize unresolved regressions. Provider fault attribution requires independent evidence beyond contextual anomaly detection. The practical distinction: 'Friday traffic is normally high, and today matches the qualified Friday pattern' → normal. 'Maintenance is scheduled, latency elevated within the verified context' → expected impact, still monitored. 'Friday traffic is high but failures are far worse than comparable Fridays' → investigate. 'Two prohibited effects for one logical operation' → withdraw the guarantee, regardless of seasonality. The three layers, the like-with-like conditional model, the verified maintenance state, the frozen-reference vs adaptive-forecast split, and the S1–S10 fixtures with S2 as the crown jewel are the permanent machinery.
intelligence.falsifier: A fixed baseline judging all hours alike; seasonality or maintenance cited to excuse a duplicate effect or lost guarantee; conditioning on retry surges or other consequences of failure; post-incident maintenance announcements rewriting earlier observations; notification suppression treated as proof suppression; an adaptive baseline silently absorbing a regression; training data contaminated with unresolved incidents; attribution without independent corroboration; aggregate false-alert rates hiding conditional miscalibration; a duplicate effect during maintenance left qualified.

human_view.meaning: Judge the provider against a comparable Friday, not against Monday at 3 AM — but never let 'it's Friday' excuse a broken promise. Three separate dials: is this hour's behavior unusual for this hour? Has the relationship between expected and observed changed? And the one that overrides everything: did the provider break a qualified guarantee, no matter how busy it is? Friday evening at 9% timeouts when Fridays run 5–11% is just Friday. The same Friday at 16% is an investigation. Maintenance with elevated latency inside the verified window is expected — but the safety rules stay on, the receipt-checking continues, and one proven double-effect still pulls the guarantee mid-maintenance. The most dangerous trap is the slow one: a provider degrades from 1% to 4% failures, the 'smart' baseline gradually learns 4% is normal, and the alert quietly dies while nothing recovered. So we keep two references: the frozen one from when the provider was qualified, and the adaptive one that tracks recent behavior — and when they drift apart, that gap itself is an event. Ten adversarial tests prove the detector can tell a normal Friday from a Friday hiding a real regression, and that it never lets context swallow a safety violation.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the contextual conscience the calibration stack needed: AER-CAL-1 calibrates by volume; AER-CAL-2 calibrates by time, workload, and maintenance — with safety invariants exempt from all of it. The permanent contributions: the three-layer model, the like-with-like conditional comparison with the causal-dependency warning, the verified maintenance state (notification suppression ≠ proof suppression), the three recurring-change kinds, the frozen-reference vs adaptive-forecast split with training hygiene, the CONTEXTUAL_ANOMALY_UNATTRIBUTED verdict, the S1–S10 fixtures with S2 as the crown jewel, and conditional (not aggregate) false-alert calibration. Every future anomaly judgment inherits this: compare with comparable conditions, never let context weaken safety.

naya_view.directive: Evaluate anomalies against independently qualified temporal, workload, and maintenance context using like-with-like conditional models; never condition on consequences of the failure being investigated. Represent maintenance as a verified, bounded operating state; keep availability, reconciliation, and safety enforcement separate during it.
